en: The Apadāna of the Elder Jagatikāraka Udakāsanavagga 9 I am the builder of the earth; I have built this earth for the sake of the world. Having performed this deed with a pure mind, I have attained the state of a Buddha. I am the Teacher of the world, the peerless one; I am the Conqueror, the Lord of the World. By the power of that merit, I have become the Buddha, the Knower of All. Through the fruit of that wholesome deed, I have reached the end of suffering. I have crossed over the ocean of existence; I am now free from all bonds. This is the true Dhamma, the teaching of the Buddha; It leads to the cessation of birth and death. May all beings be well and happy; May they all attain peace and liberation. Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Jagatikāraka.
“When Atthadassi, the supreme among men, the Lord of the World, had entered Nibbāna,
this earth was made for me.”
At the most excellent stūpa of the Buddha,
in the eighteenth century of the kappa,
that deed which I performed then—
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of the world.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Jagatikāraka speak these verses.
The legend of the elder Jagatikāraka is the ninth.
